## Trial `inter-vlan-routing-rhel10__J6Pw483`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor fully delivered the inter-VLAN routing task: node1 was given a routed interface in each VLAN (eth1 172.20.1.1/24 toward node2, eth2 172.20.2.1/24 toward node3), IP forwarding was enabled, and node2/node3 were confirmed to reach each other across the boundary via static cross-subnet routes through node1. All of this was persisted through NetworkManager profiles (node2/node3) and ifupdown/sysctl.d drop-ins (node1), and end-to-end reachability plus forwarding state were re-verified after a full, well-instrumented one-at-a-time restart of node2, node3, and node1, with clean boot-identity transitions on all three nodes matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only notable blemish is a small, unrelated, self-reverted mutation to node1's docker0 interface bundled into the main configuration command.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 50/0 (+11 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **routed-interfaces-forwarding — Satisfied:** node1 has a routed interface inside each VLAN (one facing node2's subnet, one facing node3's subnet) with IP forwarding enabled
  - **Why:** eth1 was assigned 172.20.1.1/24 (node2's VLAN) and eth2 was assigned 172.20.2.1/24 (node3's VLAN) on node1, with net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding sysctls enabled (cmd-255c391bd54c4d6e). Post-reboot state confirms both addresses and forwarding sysctls persisted (cmd-8d07c97bc2194f2c).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-255c391bd54c4d6e`, `cmd-8d07c97bc2194f2c`
- **cross-vlan-reachability — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 (each in their own subnet/VLAN behind node1) can reach each other across the VLAN boundary
  - **Why:** node2 (172.20.1.10) and node3 (172.20.2.10) each got static routes to the other's subnet via node1 (cmd-3153103097f347ec, cmd-5c23726169634d5f), and directly pinged each other successfully both immediately after configuration (cmd-cdfc123c636e4255, cmd-1308d8f3afd04e41) and again after all three nodes were rebooted (cmd-6aa13eacd1484b09, cmd-7ebe927f5fea4a8e). Gateway-level connectivity to node1's new interfaces was also verified first (cmd-3e69f040aea94985, cmd-698aa4c1952d4268).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3e69f040aea94985`, `cmd-698aa4c1952d4268`, `cmd-cdfc123c636e4255`, `cmd-1308d8f3afd04e41`, `cmd-6aa13eacd1484b09`, `cmd-7ebe927f5fea4a8e`
- **config-persistence — Satisfied:** Routing/addressing configuration is durable (not just ephemeral runtime `ip` commands)
  - **Why:** node2/node3 addressing and routes were converted to static NetworkManager profiles (cmd-de9f6fa4c05741b4, cmd-db2cd3c80f6b4e68); node1 got an ifupdown drop-in (cmd-7a08540d3d79495a) and a sysctl.d file (cmd-c7f2f93a5b844c24). All three nodes were rebooted and the addressing, routes, forwarding sysctls, and end-to-end cross-VLAN ping were re-verified afterward without manual reapplication (cmd-2b5277ca00684806, cmd-1651db7b7a6f4810, cmd-8d07c97bc2194f2c).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-de9f6fa4c05741b4`, `cmd-db2cd3c80f6b4e68`, `cmd-7a08540d3d79495a`, `cmd-c7f2f93a5b844c24`, `cmd-2b5277ca00684806`, `cmd-1651db7b7a6f4810`, `cmd-8d07c97bc2194f2c`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Command sequence was mostly clean and purposeful: discovery, targeted address/sysctl configuration, verification pings, persistence writes, and a well-executed one-at-a-time restart-evidence protocol (pre-boot-id capture, reboot, polling for reachability, post-boot-id confirmation, and re-verification of addressing/forwarding/reachability) for all three nodes in the order node2 -> node3 -> node1, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots (boot-identity changed on all three nodes between before_prepare and after_executor). One low-severity unnecessary mutation: within cmd-255c391bd54c4d6e the executor also deleted a pre-existing address (240.127.1.1/24) from docker0 and set docker0 down, an interface unrelated to the VLAN-routing task; this was bounded and self-reverted (docker0's 240.127.1.1/24 address reappeared after node1's reboot in cmd-8d07c97bc2194f2c / after_executor snapshot), so it left no lasting residue, but the deletion itself had no clear causal link to satisfying the routing requirement and should be flagged as an unneeded touch of unrelated state. No abandoned files, no executor-caused failed services (system-health.service and watchdog-control.service on node1 were already failed in the before_prepare baseline, unrelated to the executor's work), and package-health/listening-socket diffs across restarts are expected process/PID churn from the reboots rather than executor-introduced damage.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-255c391bd54c4d6e`, `cmd-8d07c97bc2194f2c`, `global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- The docker0 address deletion and its self-reversion via reboot is inferred from the initial route dump, the configuration command, and the post-reboot state snapshot rather than an explicit before/after diff isolating that single change.
- Final post-restart cross-VLAN pings (cmd-6aa13eacd1484b09, cmd-7ebe927f5fea4a8e) each showed 1 of 3 packets lost, consistent with brief ARP/neighbor re-learning right after node1's reboot rather than a persistent fault, but this transient loss is noted for completeness.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
